```{r}
source("assets/setup.R")
f <- function(x, d = 2) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = d)
m1 <- glm(f_true, data = dev, family = binomial)
dev$risk <- predict(m1, type = "response")
val$risk <- predict(m1, newdata = val, type = "response")
lpv <- qlogis(val$risk)
slope_v <- coef(glm(diabetes ~ lpv, data = val, family = binomial))[["lpv"]]
```

::: {.sheet}

## 1 · Steps (TRIPOD)

Define the **outcome, predictors and use** → check **sample size** (events!) and **missing data** → **fit** → evaluate **discrimination, calibration, usefulness** → **internal validation** (bootstrap) and **shrinkage** → **external validation**, recalibration → **report** (full equation).

Prediction ≠ explanation: aim = **accurate risks for new patients**; coefficients of correlated predictors need not be interpretable.

## 2 · Sample size

Events per parameter: **at least 10** (rule of thumb); better, use the **Riley et al.** criteria (expected R², shrinkage ≥ 0.9). Ours: **`r sum(dev$diabetes)` events**, 8 parameters (**`r f(sum(dev$diabetes) / 8, 1)` per parameter**); with 18 parameters only **`r f(sum(dev$diabetes) / 18, 1)`**.

## 3 · Discrimination

| Measure | Meaning | R |
|---|---|---|
| **AUC** | P(case ranked above non-case); 0.5 = chance | `pROC::roc()`, `auc()`, `ci.auc()` |
| Sensitivity, specificity | at a **threshold** | `table(risk >= t, y)` |
| PPV, NPV | depend on **prevalence** | same table |

Development AUC (apparent): **`r f(auc_of(dev$diabetes, dev$risk), 3)`**; age alone 0.68.

## 4 · Calibration

| Check | Ideal | R |
|---|---|---|
| **Calibration plot** (deciles) | points on the diagonal | `ntile(risk, 10)` → mean predicted vs observed |
| **Slope** | 1 (below 1 = predictions too extreme) | `glm(y ~ lp, binomial)`, `lp = qlogis(risk)` |
| **Intercept** (in the large) | 0 | `glm(y ~ offset(lp), binomial)` |
| **Brier**, scaled Brier | lower; scaled > 0 | `mean((risk - y)^2)` |

The **apparent** slope is **always 1** in the development data. Avoid the Hosmer-Lemeshow test.

## 5 · Internal validation

| Method | Comment |
|---|---|
| Apparent | **optimistic** |
| Split sample | wasteful, noisy (only for very large data) |
| **10-fold CV** | good; repeat with several fold assignments |
| **Bootstrap optimism** | corrected = apparent − mean(boot-sample performance − performance in the original data); repeat **the whole modelling process** |

Our bootstrap: optimism **0.020**, corrected AUC **0.776**; with 10 noise markers apparent **0.821**, corrected **0.779**: **no real gain**. Bootstrap **slope** 0.90 (8 predictors) and 0.80 (18).

## 6 · Shrinkage and selection

::: {.bad}
- **Stepwise / univariable selection**: unstable (noise markers chosen in 12 to 82% of bootstrap samples), biased coefficients, invalid p-values
:::

**Pre-specify** predictors. **Ridge** (`glmnet`, `alpha = 0`), **lasso** (`alpha = 1`; `lambda.1se` can over-shrink), λ by `cv.glmnet`. **Uniform shrinkage**: coefficients × bootstrap slope, re-fit the intercept.

## 7 · External validation

Our second district (2,000 adults, prevalence **`r f(100 * mean(val$diabetes), 1)`%**): AUC **`r f(auc_of(val$diabetes, val$risk), 2)`**, slope **`r f(slope_v)`**, mean predicted **`r f(100 * mean(val$risk), 1)`%** vs observed **`r f(100 * mean(val$diabetes), 1)`%**. Expect lower discrimination and **calibration drift**. **Recalibrate**: new intercept (and slope) with `glm(y ~ lp)`.

## 8 · Decision curve

net benefit = TP/n − FP/n × t/(1 − t). Compare with **treat all** and **treat none** (= 0). Choose the threshold t from **costs and benefits**. (`dcurves::dca()` or by hand.)

## 9 · Report

Data source and setting · outcome and predictors · sample size and events · missing data · **full model (intercept and coefficients)** · AUC, **calibration plot, slope, intercept** with CIs · bootstrap-corrected and **external** performance · intended use and threshold · limitations.

*The model (8 predictors, 84 events in 700 adults) had an apparent AUC of 0.80 (bootstrap-corrected 0.78); externally the AUC was `r f(auc_of(val$diabetes, val$risk), 2)` and the calibration slope `r f(slope_v)`.*

:::
